notes.title: Demo Update 0.9
notes.content: [p][b]Demo Update 0.9[/b][/p][p][/p][p]Apologies for the lengthy silence -- my time has been occupied with the beta testers, and making many changes and adjustments as EA release nears.[/p][p][/p][p]Today I'm rolling in many changes from the beta. Far from all, but those that are stable and involve the demo assets.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Changes:[/b][/p][p][/p][p][b]Significant Overhaul to rope behavior.[/b][/p][p]Ropes should now jitter less in most cases, particularly when fully reefed.[/p][p]Rope behavior should be more predictable overall, with less spastic or oscillating behavior.[/p][p]Adjusting rope length should be more stable, with less 'sproing'.[/p][p]Reefed or partially reefed sails now update to match position of moving yard more predictably.[/p][p]Made a significant overhaul to rope behavior on Tanja and Lateen rigs. This is the main change for this update. It should now be much more difficult to create physics issues by over-tightening the ropes. Essentially any rope connected to a rigid point such as the yard will now take the tautness of the connection, and other connections to the same object, into consideration. If the desired length of the rope is less than the smallest possible distance from end to end of the given rope, the applied forces will be vastly reduced.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Environment:[/b][/p][p]Disabled the rapid TOD changes on the main menu, as it outruns the GI op leading to weirdly bright appearance once the sun goes down.[/p][p]Expanded available weather types[/p][p]Added collision to some of the ground clutter on some islands[/p][p]Significant update to the starting island, including new areas and updated assets.[/p][p]Reintroduction of shoreline foam/waves[/p][p]Significantly updated xebec wreck to increase model quality[/p][p]Changed to a more complex shader for rocks on Nameless Isle and Watcher, reducing visible tiling and adding directional variation.[/p][p]Made numerous changes to possible weather types, avoiding rare cases where extreme seas (to the point where sailing is impossible and it just looked goofy) could occur.[/p][p]Added more consistent support for varied sea types. (Not just differing wave intensity, but now varied types of chop/rolling swells/etc.)[/p][p]Increased the chances of 'very rare' weather types by around 5x. This includes ashen fog and severe storms[/p][p][/p][p][b]Ships:[/b][/p][p]Moved the wind indicator on the caravel to a more visible location.[/p][p]Made several small changes to caravel ropes to try to minimize visible gaps at various rope lengths.[/p][p]Steering should feel more precise and controllable.[/p][p]Slightly reduced quality of cloth sim. Visual impact should be low relative to performance gain, though gradual collision pass through may occur earlier.[/p][p]Changed to a variable model for the Kedging system, rather than the fixed-strength system held previously.[/p][p][/p][p][b]UI:[/b][/p][p]Added a inverse zoom movement modifier to the map, allowing much faster movement when you zoom further out.[/p][p]Numerous small changes to prevent UI lockup when flipping between various menu types.[/p][p]Added visible type and destination labels to loaded cargo objects to make dealing with mixed loads/multiple tasks easier.[/p][p][/p][p][b]General:[/b][/p][p]Updated some input scripts to utilize the new input system more consistently.[/p][p]New interactable object types, with a generalized interaction interface.[/p][p]Simplified the scripting behind interaction points, to allow various types to utilize the same base class rather than fully individualized components. i.e. winches/levers/etc can now use a single tag/class rather than multiple.[/p][p]Significantly overhauled scripting behavior on interactable island objects -- this should result in substantial performance gain on some islands, particularly the Watcher.[/p][p]Lowered overall memory consumption by textures and models, and improved resource release operations.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Fixes:[/b][/p][p]Fixed a bug in the last build that led to excessive loading of meshes and textures into memory.[/p][p]Fixed some text alignment issues in some menus[/p][p]Fixed certain cargo types causing the cargo manifest to become un-interactable.[/p][p]Fixed broken text positioning on pre-existing tasks when opening the task table interface[/p][p]Fixed superfluous line breaks being added to some saved data[/p][p]Fixed event types and one time notifications being duplicated in saves, leading to oversized save files.[/p][p]Fixed excessive and drastic weather changes near Bathis.[/p][p]Fixed some poor UV unwraps[/p][p]Fixed several environment holes in several places.[/p][p]Fixed wonky textures on some store barrels[/p][p]Speculative fix for rare cases where a weird green glowing light would appear when placing cargo -- which would not disappear until reload.[/p][p]Fixed numerous superfluous nullpointer exceptions in the main menu.[/p][p][/p][p]Major update to world recentering -- that should vastly reduce system load when performing, which lead to lockup or crashing on some systems -- or the increased likelihood of physics explosions on the rigging.[/p][p][/p][p]Fixed a memory leak that could occur on some systems during weather changes.[/p][p]Fixed rare rollover on load that could affect some ships.[/p][p]Fixed an issue that could cause cargo to become impossible to unload when stacked 2 or more crates high.[/p]

notes.title: Patch 0.6.1
notes.content: [p]Patch 0.6.1[/p][p]Another patch aiming to improve both stability and performance prior to beta keys going out.[/p][p]The subscene system has been expanded to further segment out the world components. In most cases this should result in lower standby RAM usage -- though you may still experience spikes and/or brief hitches while island data is loaded in, particularly if you are running an HDD.[/p][p]I have also forced VSYNC in the background. (I plan to eventually make this a toggle feature, but for now it's in testing.) The reason for this is by normal operation the game will pile on frames until the GPU is sitting at 100%, resulting in excessive noise and heat.[/p][p]On my system (RTX 4070), GPU utilization with this patch at 1440p went from 100%-~35%.[/p][p]Other changes:[/p][p]Slightly reduced overall quality of cloth physics. Shouldn't be too noticeable, but appreciably lessens cpu load.[/p][p]Significantly overhauled many game textures, and introduced more aggressive mipmapping. This should lead to lower RAM usage and quicker loads -- though textures will appear blurry until they've loaded. This will also lower the install size.[/p][p]Fixed a major bug on the Watcher that caused significant performance impacts.[/p][p]Made numerous changes to the positional calculations of the player and ship -- this should fix unexpected behavior on loading, and lead to more predictable save/load. (If you have ever loaded only to have your ship start cosplaying as a breakdancing beluga, this is what I'm talking about.)[/p][p]Simplified many meshes to improve performance.[/p][p]Most of these changes will be most noticeable on lower end hardware -- though the game remains somewhat heavy on the cpu/gpu.[/p][p]Performance tested on Steam Deck: [/p][p]	Pre patch - FPS RANGE - ~10-20 | avg ~15[/p][p]	Post patch - FPS RANGE - ~22-60 | avg ~35[/p][p]Regarding overall development, I have received the first batch of beta keys, which will be going out within the next few weeks (or sooner). Then I anticipate a fairly short period of testing and feedback, though it could stretch longer if a lot of major issues are encountered. After that comes EA.[/p]

notes.title: Patch 0.6
notes.content: [p]In preparation for release, one of the biggest issues has been performance.[/p][p]Many of you have pointed out excessive RAM usage, as well as pc's running at 100% with screaming fans. (And not the rock concert type.)[/p][p]I believe this comes down to a Unity issue with how it stores objects in memory, even when they are not visible.[/p][p]To combat this, this patch introduces a major change to how game assets are handled. Rather than a pool of assets that are loaded in based on player proximity, each major POI has been separated into its own loaded scene. (These are layered, so there's no loading screen or anything.)[/p][p]The cons to this are you may see brief hangs during loading if you have an HDD, and there may be more noticeable pop-in -- as well as any number of bugs I haven't caught yet, so feel free to let me know if you encounter anything weird.[/p][p]The pros however should be considerable. On 0.5.7 my RAM usage ranged from 7.5GB, spiking to 20+ during asset loading on islands. On 0.6 I maintain a very consistent 2.3-2.5GB, and my pc sounds less like it's trying to take off from a runway.[/p][p]Please note that this probably won't have any impact on FPS if your system struggled before, it just reduces the RAM overhead by a significant amount.[/p]

notes.title: Hotfix 0.5.7
notes.content: [p]Hotfix 0.5.7[/p][p]Main changes:[/p][p]Overhauled spyglass and quadrant functionality.[/p][p]Both should now function more predictably, and without the strange reflection effects.[/p][p]Spyglass now has variable zoom to make focusing easier, and increased maximum zoom considerably. Both have significantly increased draw distance.[/p][p]Major Fixes:[/p][p]Fixed multiple cases that would prevent closing or interacting with Task menus.[/p][p]Fixed misaligned ghost crates that would block vision.[/p][p]Fixed most cases where a cargo item could be removed below another, leaving a hovering crate that could not be removed.[/p][p]Removed multiple cases of overdraw, which should somewhat improve performance.[/p][p]Fixed many cases of terrain geometry holes.[/p][p]Fixed missing collision of loaded cargo due to navigation clone helpers.[/p][p]Fixed floating point origin errors that prevented reliable operation. Jitter and inconsistent physics when more than 5KM from the starting island *should* be eliminated.[/p][p]Fixed numerous alignment issues for UI elements.[/p][p]Fixed some issues with world curvature that could result in unpredictable effects when loading saves.[/p][p]Significant overhaul of Zoning system, which should offer significant performance savings on larger ships.[/p][p]Numerous changes to props and smaller objects to reduce draw calls.[/p][p]Numerous script changes to reduce unnecessary calculations/operations.[/p][p]--------------[/p][p]Note on future plans:[/p][p]Barring fixes to any changes made, this is likely to be the last update to the demo for a while -- as the majority of my focus is currently on finishing up the content needed for EA release later this year.[/p]

notes.title: Hotfix 0.5.6 + Release Plans
notes.content:
Hotfix 0.5.6

Fixes: 
Missing UI prompts on ropes
Numerous terrain holes
Premature trigger instantiation due to invalid proximity checks

Changes:
Significant overhaul of character controller. Still in testing, but should feel more grounded and less bouncy. Speed has been decreased somewhat. Jumping should feel more reliable, and handling of small elevation changes should be more reliable.

Known Issues - Player can stick to walls if colliding while jumping in some cases.

Implemented world curvature for distant objects.

Overhauled world and object streaming to reduce draw calls and improve performance in most cases.

[previewyoutube=CQ3RpwrU1GQ;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

First off, one of the most consistent points of feedback I get is how the player controller is not so good. I'll admit I struggle a bit with this, probably just due to a kind of tunnel vision since I'm constantly jumping in to test different stuff I don't really register any issues.

In short, the updated version implements considerably more drag, reduces speed, and is much less slippery, so you won't be Tony Hawking off every little bump in the terrain. Jumping should be more consistent as well, allowing more function disembarks. There are a couple known issues I'm still working on -- the character is more likely to get stuck on abrupt elevation changes, and can kind of stick to walls a bit in some cases -- but before I dump another week into fine tuning, I want to see if players like the way it's going.

This update will also introduce a number of changes to scripts, assets, and world asset management, that should reduce draw calls significantly in most cases, as well as reduce unnecessary script operations that should save a few ms here and there.

I have also implemented world curvature. This is somewhat exaggerated, as with the relatively low distances between islands, a realistic figure wasn't really noticeable. For context, the spawn point is only about 3.5K from the 300m tall watcher. So at eye level I napkin mathed that to be around .8 m of drop, which isn't really visible. I've increased this by 5x -- so it's at least noticeable, especially on more distant islands like Bathis, which drops around 50m from the spawn point.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Next up, new ship time. Filling the role of Caelean 'starter' ship, is the Padewakang. This is a simple, dependable vessel, the design differs from other Calean ships, as (in the game world) these are the signature ships of a Caelean Vassal state, that operated on huge inland lakes. The design survived due to being simpler to build and maintain than the more ornate junk style hulls.

This will have twin boomed rectangular sails, that function almost as a cross between lateen and battened sails. It will also be steered via twin steering oars rather than a conventional rudder. It will be larger than the Caravel, but less capable in weather, and quite slow.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
lastly, a little about my plans for release. With so many variables in play, I feel it might lessen the bugfix and tuning race some with simply fewer things to test. That said, I do worry about leaving a sour taste with a buggy experience that doesn't have a lot of content.

My aim right now is to release later this year, with the following:

6 playable ships, with three from each of the major in game cultures and their vassals. At least three more are planned for both existing cultures and others not currently represented.

Apart from ships, there are currently 7 islands planned to be present at launch -- with quite a few more expected later on. This number does not include a handful of 'special' locations.

In terms of features that are planned, but will probably not be present, or very incomplete, at the time of launch -- the main gameplay elements are:

1. Fast travel (This will function sort of similarly to overworld map gameplay such as those seen in games like Owlcat's pathfinder series, and many older rpgs.) That is you are not picking a destination and teleporting there, rather going a distance will cost time and provisions, especially on larger ships.

2. Encounters. Accompanying the above, these will be semi-random events that can interrupt fast travel. These could be other ships, special weather events, or any kind of more tailored experience that isn't practical for general open world appearance.

3. Combat. A degree of this is planned, but there are many decisions to make before I talk about it too much.

4. Ship modification. This will be a somewhat limited affair -- but I do plan for the shipyard to offer hull and rigging changes for some ships. This won't be as flexible or complex as the kind of modifications possible in games like Sailwind. Rather I plan on allowing things like specific rig conversions, so a Caravel with a square mainsail + headsail, that sort of thing. More like flipping between ship variants than having full customization control.

5. Story progression. Will get more into this another time.

notes.title: Following Seas - Performance Enhancements
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=dF4h9jFetkE;full][/previewyoutube]

Hello

Significant update here. I think everyone who has tried the demo has experienced frustration with performance issues. And while I recognize that premature optimization can be the bane of many projects, there's also the fact that building in performant structures early can save a lot of headaches later down the line.

The first big change is a significant expansion of the zoning system.  While ships in following seas are single root rigidbodies, there are hundreds to thousands of different assets making them up. This is further complicated by different audio and lighting zones, all of which are dynamic, which as a performance cost.

In previous updates, ships were segregated into interior and exterior spaces to reduce the overhead, but this still had issues, especially on larger ships. Now, zones have been moved from box zones to much more precise mesh based zones, allowing for more, and more precise zones to be created.

Additionally, 'non-zone' groupings have been added as well, essentially meaning many ship assets will stop drawing when the player is in a zone, as opposed to the reverse. Essentially high cost objects like the rigging and deck fixings can stop drawing when the player is below deck. Overall, this will have varied effects, depending on the ship. The caravel for example only has one zone, and will see no real improvements. The Saettia, as seen in the intro, has essentially five. This change allows for much more clutter and visual detail, while substantially cutting down on draw calls. Typically from many thousands per frame, to a few hundred, while still keeping the advantage of dynamic, non-batched meshes, and heavy LOD use.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The next change will be interesting. The cloth system is by a wide margin the most expensive element of the simulation. There's only so much that can be done to improve this without cutting quality to an unsatisfying degree -- but this update sees a speculative change that may result in substantial improvement for some. (But it might also make things worse) So I will be pushing this out shortly, and would appreciate any feedback on whether performance improves. Additionally, this change *should* result in significantly lowered changes of particle explosions, depenetration loops, and physics death spirals resulting in crashes. Essentially the cloth sim is now asynchronous and multithreaded, and the bulk of the work has been moved from the CPU to a GPU based system. (Hence why the results may be very dependent on your system.)

On the steam deck for example, my performance in the intro has gone from slideshow to fully playable -- while on my main PC it actually loses performance as I have a strong CPU.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

As for other changes, I've overhauled whipstaff steering, so it should feel a bit more precise and reliable, while still hopefully giving the impression that it's a stick on a rope.

I've added a percentage display to the reefing UI to make it easier to judge position without jumping to exterior views.

I've replaced the crosshair with a much smaller indicator.

And I've made numerous small changes to ship and prop objects, mostly with the aim to reduce materials and draw calls, as well as getting rid of some of the remaining placeholder spheres.

notes.title: Following Seas - Distant Shores
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=01tHoGKCWGw;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

Small update, I had a more substantial update planned, but lost a chunk of progress due to pc issues, and had to roll back to a backup. Nothing major, just a few hours lost.

In the meantime, I've been working on more landmarks, some of which are being kept under wraps, but I felt this one is worth showing. So far all islands have been using the Imperial building set, but this is only one of the cultures present in the area. The other being Caelean. If you aren't following the project, this is a bit of a fusion of cultures with a heavy visual leaning on Asian cultures.

I understand that might come off as a bit dismissive, as I'm aware that there are vast nuances and varieties across time and place, but I'm not a historian, and am not aiming to recreate culture, rather more a visual style. Much in the same way the Imperial culture borrows heavily from India, the Barbary States, and the Iberian peninsula.

In game this aims to be a challenging port, being well protected and very tight for large ships. It will be the largest remaining settlement still under direct Caelean control, as their homelands have completely fallen, and most of the remaining survivors have splintered into new groups, such as the reclusive people of the Watcher. This island is in disrepair, and struggling due to lack of resources. The island is fairly large, but has poor soil and very little plant life -- along with no fresh water, leaving the inhabitants dependent on a shrinking number of seaworthy ships to supply them with goods.

This aims to be a major trading port, as well as the only place to build or buy Calean ships. There is still a lot of detailing to do, but it's in a state where the initial structure is present. I haven't settled on exactly where this island will be located, but likely significantly north of any present islands. Be aware that some of the assets are placeholder, particularly banners and symbols, as they are not representative of the ingame culture.

notes.title: Untitled
notes.content:
A small update has been added to the demo:

Hotfix 0.5.2

Fixes:

Numerous small fixes to geometry, colliders, and animations.
Fixes several terrain issues with the watcher, plugging holes and fixing tearing.
Fix for shore waves causing holes in the water, or visual distortions.

Changes:

Majorly overhauled player controller. Shouldn't feel too different, but the backend has been altered to decouple player movement from the ship's rigidbody, allowing smoother motion overall, and less jitter or sliding. Please be aware that due to the scope of this change, some unintended issues may be present.

Reduced headbob by around 60%.

Additionally, I've posted a new video going over the changes and updates to the upcoming junk rigged ships.

It's been a long time since I've focused on mechanics surrounding junk rigs. They had fallen behind after all the updates and feedback early in the demo -- and a big progress blocker has been updating the logic and controls of the rig to the newer aerodynamic model used for the lateen sails. It's finally time to showcase a bit of how this is coming along.

Additionally I've done a detail pass on the Caelean Junk, adding new details and effects. All ships will now see more complex zoned audio as well, further distinguishing exterior and interior spaces.

Control over battened sails is now much more controllable. Moving the base rope functions similarly to how it does for the lateen rig, but controlling length is now a two stage process. Mousewheel controls length as it does for lateens, but once the rope is fully tight, it will move to controlling the lines to each batten, essentially allowing you to allow the rig to be more or less rigid. This is especially useful if you want to sail laterally or reverse.

As they are similar in size, the Caelean junk is easy to compare to the Xebec. The aim is for the Junk to be somewhat slower, but more seaworthy and able to carry larger loads. The hull is split by multiple bulkheads as with historic junks, though not nearly as many as that would make traversal a bit annoying.

notes.title: Major Update
notes.content:
Many of you will have noticed that no updates have come to the demo in quite some time.

This is not due to any stoppage in progress, rather most of the progress in the last few months has focused on content that simply isn't present in the demo, or content and mechanics that are simply not ready for consumption.

That said, there remains numerous serious issues with the demo, and given that a major purpose of the demo is to gather feedback and testing -- I've made the decision to release a major update. This may include more features in the future, but right now the main features and changes in the demo are as follows:

Changes:

The intro segment remains, but has been overhauled somewhat. The ship should now sink much more quickly, and in a more predictable way to help make it clear to the player that saving the vessel is not possible. Additional details and chaos has been added, and the reef is now visible to the player.

Many small assets have been added to the world, including more cultural changes such as different rowboat and lantern styles for different culture ships.

Much of the UI has been overhauled to hopefully be clearer and nicer to look at.

Handheld tools now have more consistent overlays and viewports.

Significant overhauls to lighting, physics, particle effects, and global reflections to improve visuals and remove strange artifacts and pop in.

Increased draw distances significantly.

Crew control menu has been added (TAB - but not used in the demo as no crew is present, however you can get an idea of how it will work.)

The map has been replaced with a more capable and readable interface. Additionally the space between landmarks has been increased.

Some tools now include additional controls to tag current readings to make it easier to remember when plotting on the map.

Ship zones are more sectionalized, allowing asset drawing to skip when you wouldn't be able to see them -- significantly reducing draw calls in some cases.

Task menus now include the option to buy provisions directly, or to purchase materials with which to build ships. (Note -- this feature is disabled for the demo as no shipyards are present.)

Weather lifetime has been reduced to allow more frequent weather changes, and weather can now include various sea-states. (Previously wave intensity could vary, but always utilized the same base wave structure -- now you may see smoother rolling seas, or more choppy states.)

Fixes:

Numerous minor bugfixes -- too many to list.
Fixed serious issue that could cause ship to rotate or capsize while interacting with the map.
Fixed serious issue that could cause ocean chunks to visibly disappear. 
Fixed serious issue that could cause ship to start and stop repeatedly.

Please note that due to significant backend changes, new bugs have likely been added, and in some cases saves from previous versions may be affected.

notes.title: Still alive, even if the crew isn't.
notes.content:
Apologies for the lengthy delay. There's been a death in the family, along with some personal struggles.

That said, development is progressing steadily.

I would like to introduce the Epitaphs. These are among the first overtly fantasy elements added, and I'd like to give a bit of an explanation as to what they are, and why I'm introducing them now.

While the world of Following Seas aims to be grounded in many areas, types of magic do exist. A big practitioner of these arts (prior to the collapse at least) was the Caelean culture. A cost of this is a struggle to maintain population numbers for reasons that may become clearer later -- but ultimately the effects of this were a somewhat distinct attitude towards death. Rather than practicing burial, or burnings as the Imperials do, instead bodies of (some) of the dead are ritualistically prepared, and animated. They are draped in ribbons, bearing texts that tell the story of who they were in life, their families, and notable events from their life.

Their purpose is to both act as walking gravestones, and to provide service in death to their descendants and people. Don't think of them as zombies or rotting corpses. They are closer to mummies, they don't stink or moan or eat brains or anything. In gameplay they function basically as robots that can automate some of your ship controls.

With all that said, these are intended to be the first kind of crew available to the player. I would like to expand this to include more varied human crew members eventually, but I'm not the best character artist or animator -- and these offer a simpler approach from a design perspective, and I feel have potential to be a bit interesting from a story perspective.

At this point, their capabilities are pretty limited, but more is intended, as well as a gradual dejankification. (Have I mentioned I'm not much of an animator?).

Commands can be issued from a radial menu, and currently allow for sail controls and pumping. An Epitaph can be directed to continually work the pumps until told differently, or you can queue up orders to manage the sails, furling or unfurling to any value without you needing to leave the helm. Soon to be added is capstan/windlass control, which aims to make precise harbour maneuvers easier, especially on the larger ships, as you can place the kedging anchor repeatedly without needing to wind it yourself.

You will be able to have multiple Epitaphs on a ship, but for practicalities sake don't expect realistic crew numbers. Each ship will have a preset number of crew stations, likely  not exceeding a dozen or so for the bigger ships.[previewyoutube=ntpaenmcEj4;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Following Seas - Map and Navigation Updates
notes.content:
First video of 2025.

Those of you active on the discord will have seen much of this before, but for everyone else, a major component that I've been working on in the background is a change to the navigation and map system. I remain a little torn, as I like the idea of a fully physicalized map like the one present in the demo. However, such a map has a number of issues, mostly stemming from scaling issues, and visibility issues from lighting artifacts and clutter.

Based on feedback from the fine folks at discord, I will not be eliminating this map or its basic functionality. However, I'm moving most of the complex functions to a new menu. You'll still be able to view the map, and apply long and lat measurements -- but triangulation, plotting, and waypoint systems, along with the upcoming fast travel system, will be accessed from this new screen.

This brings scalability, and significant backend improvements to allow for more dynamic point of interest placements. Through a radial menu you can create any number of plots, with as many waypoints as you like. For example you could create a desired course, and have a second plot tracking your actual position based on triangulation or positional calculations. To add to this, the navigational tools are in the process of gaining some extra functionality. You can mark the current measurement of each tool, which will be referenced on the map so that it's easier for you to remember. Note that it is up to you to determine if those outputs are correct, it simply references the current values.

Triangulation has been overhauled as well. You can place the cursor over the desired reference point, and then the mouse position will determine the reverse angle to indicate direction to the measurement point. You can do this from as many reference points as you like to get more precise positional data.

Panning and zooming are also now supported.

Note that these features are not present in the demo due to some dependencies.

[previewyoutube=d3d8pAKuq6Q;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Development Progress - Xebec, Sampan, and Shipyard
notes.content:
Lots to go over in this update.

I know things have been quiet with the demo for a while -- this is not because of reduced development or abandonment or anything like that. Mainly I feel I've got it in a mostly functional state, and the bulk of work has moved on to new content. That said I am working on a patch to fix a few issues, and add a bit of functionality, some of which will be covered in this video.

A big blocker for early access naturally is that you need more ships. So a big piece of work lately has been on taking all the developments, changes, and systems developed through the demo, and applying them to the other ships. The Xebec is the main target of this currently -- and she's mostly been converted to the new sailing system, along with some minor model changes.

With this development, I'm well into a first pass at a shipyard system. How this will work is that you will need to either find a wreck in the world, or find somewhere to gain drawings of the ship in question, and then deliver these plans to a shipyard capable of building the given ship. This is intended to be a mostly culture based thing -- so Imperial ships can only be built at a port familiar with the construction methods.

Once the plans are delivered, there's a few ways to proceed. If you are flush with cash -- you can simply purchase the ship outright, but the costs will be high. The other method is a much smaller payment, with you supplying the construction materials yourself.

To make this work also required an overhaul to the contracts system, which was previously called tasks. While you can still take on contracts as normal, you can also purchase some goods outright, and transport them to the shipyard. The option to sell, plus regionalized/demand pricing is expected in the future. Another addition that goes along with this, is that you can both buy and sell provisions at ports as well -- so you won't get overloaded with oil any longer.

Building a ship is intended to be a slow process, so you don't have to deliver all goods at once -- you can deliver piecemeal, or make partial payments. I'm toying with the idea of having a visual staged contruction of each ship -- but that's a big project so I haven't decided.

You won't lose your existing ship -- but due to the scripting demands of playable ships, I expect only one will be active at a time, with the other going into storage. I know many people have been asking about customization, and I expect that this will happen at the shipyard as well. Don't expect full on sail by sail customization -- but I'm toying with the idea of preset rigging variants instead. Think of a xebec with mixed square and lateen sails, or caravel with bowsprit and headsail, etc. I'd like to add things like hull and sail colors, flags, figureheads, etc as well, but that's long term.[previewyoutube=_yTMuB_KZWw;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Hotfix 11
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=aSJ9xhffHy0;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

Smaller update here. As bugs are fixed I will be winding down updates to the demo. (Not entirely, but work is moving back towards new content.)

This update hopefully sees a fix for cases where using the map would case a capsize event. Additionally, a major overhaul has been made to the game world, implementing cell based culling. This should see minor to major fps increases, depending on your system.

For example with max settings in 1440p on my system, average fps on the starter island moved from 45-55 to 95-130. These figures may not be typical, but there should be few, if any, cases where performance is worse with this method.

You may see the occasional larger-scale pop in, or some texture/mesh bugs in the world introduced by this, but I am working on them as I find them.

notes.title: Hotfix 10.1
notes.content:
Apologies to all -- there was an issue with the most recent hotfix that would prevent interaction with certain ship elements on starting a new game.

Just pushing out a quick fix -- no new content but the following issues should be sorted:

Can now interact with the tutorial items for provisions and sail control.

Sail physics should be more resistant to explosive movements that were introduced with the new sail controls -- particularly on lower end systems.

notes.title: Hotfix 10
notes.content:
Another set of fixes and changes.

Should now have finally solved the duplicate manifest issue some players experienced. Additionally dynamic movement should be back for handheld items.

Made a number of backend changes to render layers and draw distances to hopefully improve performance, while also increasing the distance at which large distant objects and landmasses can be seen.

Made a number of changes to the sail mirroring process during yard switching. Should now mirror more reliably without overpenetration.

Replaced most visible ropes on the caravel with a shader based solution. This is very much in testing, and you will likely encounter occasional physics explosions or other issues, or excessively stretchy/floppy behavior. The benefit is a reduced CPU load, and somewhat less of a noodly look for interactable ropes.

Removed the additional rope to the sail corners, replacing with a linked rope setup which is supported through the new solution.

Made a number of mesh changes to Caravel sails to reduce clipping and visual artifacts.

Ballast is now positional, and can be shifted at will. The effect this has on stability is still being refined, so you may see excessive heel or movement when shifting in some directions.

A number of small changes have been made to shadows and reflections, aiming to slightly improve performance without sacrificing quality.

notes.title: Hotfix 9
notes.content:
Apologies for the long silence.

Smaller update today, but includes some larger features.

First off is some tuning to the sail reefing mechanic, that allows sailcloth to compress much more than previous, which should allow for a cleaner look when reefed.

Fixed some issues regarding reef calculations that would result in 0 thrust at partial reef.

Added an additional rope to the forward corner of the mainsail to allow for finer control. (In testing so not added to the rear.)

Speculative fix for some remaining cases of physics explosions when moving ropes to distant cleats.

Added a first iteration of a yard switching mechanic. Currently this can be done from the reefing winch. Simply pressing 'r' will perform the switch. Can be done with the sail in any position, but when done reefed you may encounter more clipping and depenetration jitter. Note that this is primarily to test the effectiveness of switching -- the presumed future solution will be more involved than a simple key press.

Performed a significant dejankification pass on the rowboat, though a fair bit remains. You should find more control, particularly in turns. Holding lshift, or whatever sprint is bound to will allow for reverse turning and travel. Known issues are poor performance in rough seas, and frequent bow dives that can cause water clipping and loss of speed.

You can now hold up to 6 provision/loot barrels on the rowboat, where they will snap into position, preventing most physics problems.

Have yet to determine the odd hull movements some users experience when using the map -- working on it.

notes.title: Hotfix 8
notes.content:
Another day another hotfix, though some new content as well.

Further changed the kedging system to hopefully behave a little more predictably. Proper forward torque is back, but a fair bit of damping has been applied. Ship will accelerate more slowly under anchor forces, and shouldn't wildly swing around anymore. Might be a touch slow, so opinions appreciated.

Slightly increased the tautness of cloth -- but there's practical limits here that kind of reduce how much I can do.

Added a heavy dampening effect to the spars when under higher sail loads -- will reduce the amount of floppage when under sail a fair bit, though not entirely.

Rudder should now work as expected while reversing.

Made a number of minor changes to sailing -- increased possible speeds, reduced bow->stern heel, and fiddled with some variables. Still not quite where I'd like it, there's some angles that should perform better than they currently do, but getting closer. Your thoughts and comments are much appreciated.

Fixed some serious bugs that would result in sudden deceleration, or the inability to move forwards -- particularly when running.

Made some (currently wip) changes to sail audio. Flapping cloth sounds will now decrease as  wind fills and tightens the sail. As speed increases whistling and buffeting of the rigging will be audible. Note that this is a bit loud from interior spaces, but curious how it feels for you all.

Added the ability to move cargo while underway -- along with tweaking the UI for placing cargo. In addition to placing and removal, you can now select a single block via alt-left click, and then move that block to any (empty) space.

For a more detailed overview of the sailing changes made in the last two updates, as well as some new content, please enjoy this long and meandering video.

[previewyoutube=-CcQUghc1Tg;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Hotfix 7
notes.content:
Yet another hotfix.

Fixes a few more issues with the updated sailing model, particularly with regard to close reach and close hauled sailing. Attainable speeds should be much higher in these positions.

Other changes:

Ultrawide support!

Most non standard resolutions should now work, as long as they are in landscape format.

Many small changes have been made to UI elements to support varied resolutions.

Reworked the task UI to be more readable.

Even more speculative changes to prevent the Junk from becoming inappropriately intimate with the dock.

Moved the kedge anchor point (meaning where the pulling forces are applied) to a more central position. This should result in smoother motions, but will apply less turning torque on the hull.

Plugged some collider holes on the Watcher.

Flags and ribbons located in the world should now align with wind direction.

Significantly increased variability of wind direction.

notes.title: Hotfix 6.2
notes.content:
Another small hotfix.

Hopeful that it will fix the sudden start/stopping that many players are encountering. Unclear if this is related to the longer full stops that some have mentioned, but we shall see.

Other changes:

Radically increased ship momentum. Under good winds it can take up to two minutes to reach 'top' speed, so if you don't seem to go anywhere, just give it a short while. (I intend to make this persistent later). The flip side of this is that the hull will maintain gained speed for similar times, so this should make it easier to maintain speed through turns or while tacking.

Decreased heel forces caused by the rudder by 50%.

Should now be able to maintain at least some performance with just one sail.

Fixed some (most?) cases where inverting yard position relative to hull could cause inverted heel direction in some cases.

notes.title: Hotfix 6.1
notes.content:
Apologies to all, as I had to rollback hotfix 6 to fix some major issues.

Trying this again. Fixed some of the biggest issues with the (new) sailing system.

Fairly certain that there are plenty of fresh new issues to discover, but I think it's closer to testable now.

All previously mentioned changes are still in, with a couple additional ones.

1 -- COG has been lowered somewhat, resulting in a more stable hull in most situations. However, lateral wind forces have been raised somewhat to account for wind against the sail rather than hull -- so you still need to watch out. The hull should list much less when turning.

2 -- Apparent wind has been implemented. As hull speed increases, the visual angle of the wind will shift to account. This may require adjustment to the sails at speed, as the wind may move inline with the sails position causing them to flatten.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44937817/4b5e3c93a606d823ec69054278023ec136208ff0.png[/img]

For example in the above image, the ship is moving forward at 2.5 units/s, (yellow line), while the wind (pink line) is at 8 units/s. Light blue is the angle of the apparent wind.

Other changes:

Fixed issues related to boarding the ship from the rowboat causing strange behavior.

Fixed issue where rowboat couldn't be retrieved in some cases.

Fixed crouching while fishing causing you to fall off.

Fixed cases where the player being knocked from the platform while fishing would lock player in the fishing state.

Fixed cursor disappearing when opening the menu while interacting with the map.

There are likely to be issues relating to the sailing changes, so I appreciate your comments, and will get to fixing things as soon as I'm able.

notes.title: Hotfix 6
notes.content:
Finally a new hotfix should be live within the next hour or two.

The list of changes isn't huge, but are generally more substantial than prior fixes.

----------------------------------

Added rudder angle readout to helm.

Reworked the kedge anchor to apply force more strongly, over shorter distances. This should make it easier to move the hull short distances, and no longer require placement of the anchor to be near the maximum allowable length.

Further increased mouse sensitivity options.

Added global volume slider. This is the first stage of more complex audio options, right now just controls the volume of all audio -- which should help the multi app folks.

Started some UI layout and design changes to support eventual text scaling.

Fixed ladder interactions when using non-standard keyboard axis setups.

Significantly overhauled the function and calculations behind lateen sails based on feedback. This is likely to introduce some new issues, as it is a significant change, so you thoughts would be appreciated. (Though I'd still like to stress that the aim here isn't 100% realism, though I'd like to be serviceable.)

These changes can be broken down into the following areas:

1 - Chord and Aspect ratio.

The chord of the sail is now measured from a top down view, along with the aspect ratio, and the position of thickest chord relative to chord span.
The aim is to roll this in to AOA tracking, but for now it is used to generate a dampening effect when the aspect ratio is too high or too low.
This means a full flat sail will generate no lift, and high thickness to chord ratio will significantly degrade performance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44937817/d7813d9961f3e51f8617d179d432e7e80fbc9d0f.png[/img]

2 – Thrust

Thrust is now calculated based on each sail’s chord line, along with the thrust potential of each sail. This also accounts for hull direction and velocity. This allows for lateral and sternward motion, accounting for the increased drag on the hull. As forward speed increases (relative to hull), the lateral forces are dampened by the keel, resulting in straighter motion.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44937817/e96bae5db6dda30f5fee991383f3b9073d919247.png[/img]

For example in image-2, the hull is stationary. (Ignore sail placement, as I left them in their default position)
Green represents the direction of the wind coming from starboard, with the wind deflecting off the chord line towards the stern.
Blue represents the thrust direction being applied to the hull for each sail.
Yellow represents the same, but accounting for keel forces. (currently 0 as hull is stationary.)
This means the ship will be driven mostly to port, without making much headway.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44937817/246805938982a2ccb707ca153b2cdad9276b5722.png[/img]

Now in image-3, the ship is moving forward at a fairly high speed.
Colors represent the same, but in this case the Yellow thrust lines have moved inline with the keel due to hydrodynamic forces, resulting in mostly stable forward thrust.

3—Heel

Heel is also now calculated per each sail, affected by the relative strength of each sail. Additionally, heel direction and intensity is based upon a sail’s chord line relative to the wind, without focusing on the orientation of the hull or yard. This should result in more predictable outcomes, particularly when the sail/yard are at extreme angles.

Stability may be excessively effected by this -- currently making adjustments.

notes.title: Hotfix 5.1
notes.content:
Very small hotfix due to reports of some bugs introduced by my last hotfix. Length control should now work for all ropes, instead of fore only.

Lanterns are now persistent.

One user has indicated that in the last couple patches the ship can no longer move, and is anchored in place.

I'm not able to replicate, and logs didn't elucidate. Please let me know if the occurs for anyone, as that may help me pin down the issue.

notes.title: Hotfix 5
notes.content:
One more for the Thanksgiving (CA) weekend. Small list of fixes, but wanted to get a few final things sorted prior to Steam's Next Fest starting tomorrow.

Fixed bug that would prevent unloading of final task item, or fail to reward player on task completion in many cases. (Thanks for the save files on this one, allowed me to finally pin down the cause.)

Fixed most cases in which over-retraction of ropes would cause physics explosion.

Crapified Saettia sails to better indicate that trying to use them is pointless.

Prevent Player being able to climb down through hull using ladders.

Made Ballast persistent between saves.

*hopeful* fix for occastional CTD caused by a NAN exception when reducing ballast to 0.

Next patch should include fixes for persistent lights and some big collider issues on land.

notes.title: Hotfix 4
notes.content:
Apologies for the delay, a couple of these issues were tougher to deal with than expected.

Smaller list of fixes today -- but more substantial on the backend.

Rewrote the crouch/crawl logic. Should be much more reliable now. Note that you may be able to find some holes in the ship colliders, as I haven't fully updated them to account for tiny player. In extreme seas there may be some jitter as well -- still working on cleaning that up.

Significantly overhauled the heel logic for lateen sails. *Should* be more reliable, and no longer result in reverse heel from what is expected.

Mooring ropes should now be persistent, and should properly apply force on reload.

Significantly overhauled the behavior of yards on lateen sails, should be more predictable in movement, and less likely to 'explode' causing ctd.

Added an option to skip the intro sinking scene. (Hold interact once loaded)

Made a number of speculative changes to the object drift some players experience. I've not been able to replicate this issue, so has been difficult to diagnose. Currently only masts and cleats have been altered -- but I would appreciate letting me know if you still experience issues, or if any new and horrible behavior is witnessed.

Also would be interested if any dramatic performance changes are noted -- as I've cranked up the physics iterations a bit to hopefully reduce explosive depenetration on jointed objects.

Fixed a bug with tasks related to variable player origin -- that would cause the task to regard the player as being either too far or too close in some cases. Unclear if this was also the cause of the inability for some players to receive rewards, but hopefully. (Another one I've not been able to reproduce -- but I'm working on it.)

Increased ship inertia significantly, should be slower to accelerate, and maintain speed longer. (Still much quicker than reality -- but don't want to slow things down too much.)

These changes won't effect your saves, but due to the amount of changes to physics objects, it may cause some unintended behavior, so comments are appreciated if you run into anything weird. I'll continue working through the weekend, though I'm stuck transporting relatives so will be out of town off and on.

notes.title: Hotfix 3
notes.content:
Fixes and Changes:

Change how sail performance is calculated in multi-sail setups. Previously each sail contributed a range of values, and overall effectiveness was averaged between them. This meant that cases where a single small sail was fouled or reefed could drastically reduce the effectiveness of the mainsail.

Now sails contribute additively within clamped ranges, so small sails will still contribute less -- but you can sail fine with one or more (depending on ship) reefed.

-----

Provisioning Dialog now shows your current money balance.

-----

Added a simplified menu to the opening scene, allowing user to quit or return to menu, and providing a note to make it clear what is happening.

-----

Fixed some missing colliders on the starting island.

-----

Hopeful fix for certain cases in which player could get stuck crouching

-----

Added wider range of mouse sensitivity

-----

Reduced stamina loss while swimming

-----

Added Sky and Environment quality presets. Depending on your system this may have huge impacts. My work pc dropped GPU utilization from ~80% to ~18% on low.

-----

Increased swimming force applied to upstroke, you may now cosplay as a dolphin

-----

Added invert mouseX/Y checkboxes to the settings

-----

Fixed mouse sensitivity options not applying to external view

-----

Added more cleats to the aft half of the caravel

-----

Added interactable item in place of missing rowboat to make it clearer where to interact to retrieve lost rowboats

-----

Speed on foot off ship should be more consistent

-----

Changed some descriptions on the store page to make it clearer that this game is in a pre-alpha state.

-----

Fixed a major issue with the task system. You may have noticed an inability to complete tasks if you saved and loaded after accepting. This was due to the change to variable origin for world center. Tasks still relied on absolute positions, which would break on world recentering.

Tasks should now be much more reliable.

-----

Fixed an issue where when having multiple active tasks, you could unload any cargo to count towards the target of the selected task.

------

Unfortunately, this update will break your saves if you have cargo aboard, or any active tasks.


I won't be around much tomorrow as I have an urgent event a few hours away, but I'll continue working as I can. Your patience and bug catching have been much appreciated.
